table.name: foreign_data
table.purpose: Localized (non-English) card data for a Magic: The Gathering card database. One row per card per language/printing, holding the translated name, rules text, flavor text and type line, plus the language and the printing's Gatherer multiverseid. Each row links back to a card in `cards` via `uuid` (many foreign rows per card). Empty strings (rather than NULLs) are used when a card has no text/flavor/type in that language, and some rows exist only as stubs (name only, no multiverseid).

flavorText.name: flavorText
flavorText.description: The card's flavor text translated into the row's language (e.g. German, Japanese, Spanish, French, Russian, Korean, Portuguese). Empty string when the printing has no flavor text (~44% of rows).

id.name: id
id.description: Surrogate primary key / row identifier for this table (sequential integers 1–229205, one per row). The statistically accepted joins to cards.tcgplayerProductId, cards.cardKingdomId, cards.cardKingdomFoilId and cards.mcmMetaId are almost certainly coincidental numeric overlaps with unrelated vendor product IDs, not real relationships.

language.name: language
language.description: Human-readable name of the language this localization is in. 16 values: the core MTG languages (Japanese, French, German, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian, Korean, Chinese) plus rare promotional ones (Ancient Greek, Sanskrit, Latin, Hebrew, etc.).

multiverseid.name: multiverseid
multiverseid.description: The Gatherer 'multiverseid' of this specific foreign-language printing (Wizards of the Coast's identifier for an individual printed card). NULL for ~17% of rows — printings not catalogued in Gatherer (e.g. promotional or stub entries). Nearly unique per row, with a handful of duplicates.

name.name: name
name.description: The card's name translated into the row's language (e.g. 'Zyklop vom Blutfelsen', '霊紋の振り子', 'Pacifismo'). Repeats reflect common cards printed in many languages/sets.

text.name: text
text.description: The card's rules/abilities text in the row's language, with line breaks and mana/reminder notation preserved. Empty string for cards with no rules text (~16% of rows).

type.name: type
type.description: The card's type line translated into the row's language (e.g. 'Kreatur — Zyklop' = Creature — Cyclops, 'Criatura Lendária — Guerreiro Goblin' = Legendary Creature — Goblin Warrior). Empty string when the type line was not localized for that printing.

uuid.name: uuid
uuid.description: Foreign key to cards.uuid identifying the (English) card/face whose localization this row holds. Many-to-one: a card typically has one row per language (up to ~10 rows share a uuid; 34,056 distinct cards across 229,186 rows).

table.name: legalities
table.purpose: One row per card printing per Magic: The Gathering format, stating whether that card is Legal, Banned or Restricted in that format. This is the standard MTGJSON-style legalities table accompanying the cards/sets/rulings tables: 55,608 distinct cards (uuid) x up to 15 formats = 427,907 rows.

format.name: format
format.description: Magic: The Gathering tournament format in which the card's legality is recorded. The 15 distinct values are MTG format slugs: commander, legacy, vintage, duel (Duel Commander), modern, pioneer, pauper, penny (Penny Dreadful), premodern, etc. Eternal formats (commander/legacy/vintage, ~55,576 rows each) have an entry for essentially every card, while narrower formats like modern (40,774) only cover cards relevant to them.

id.name: id
id.description: Synthetic auto-increment surrogate key (primary key) for the legality row. Values run 1–427,907 with a perfectly uniform distribution (min 1, max 427,907, mean = median), i.e. it is just a row number and carries no business meaning. The accepted joins to cards.mcmId, cards.mcmMetaId, cards.cardKingdomId, cards.cardKingdomFoilId and cards.tcgplayerProductId are coincidental numeric matches against a dense integer range, not real relationships.

status.name: status
status.description: Legality of the card in the row's format: 'Legal' (playable, normal 4-copy limit; 424,958 rows), 'Banned' (not playable in that format; 2,313 rows), 'Restricted' (playable but limited to a single copy — a rule Magic: The Gathering uses in Vintage; 636 rows, a high count because each restricted card has many printings, each with its own uuid/row).

uuid.name: uuid
uuid.description: Foreign key to cards.uuid: the unique identifier (MTGJSON-style v5 UUID) of the card printing whose legality this row records. Each uuid appears up to 15 times, once per format (55,608 distinct cards across 427,907 card–format rows), confirming the many-to-one relationship to the cards table.

table.name: rulings
table.purpose: Official Magic: The Gathering card rulings (rules clarifications/Oracle rulings issued by Wizards of the Coast), one row per ruling attached to a specific card printing. Evidence: ruling texts use MTG rules vocabulary (cycling, totem armor, Adventure spells, planeswalkers, unearth, Slivers), the uuid column joins to cards.uuid, and the sibling tables (cards, sets, legalities, foreign_data, set_translations) match the MTGJSON database layout. The same ruling text repeats across rows because it is attached to every printing of the same card, which is why text and date have low uniqueness relative to row count.

date.name: ruling_date
date.description: Date the ruling was issued/published, in YYYY-MM-DD form. Only 109 distinct dates over ~88k rows, with large batches (e.g. 6,334 rulings on 2004-10-04, 4,123 on 2021-02-05) corresponding to bulk ruling releases that accompany Comprehensive Rules updates; range 2004-10-04 to 2021-02-05.

id.name: ruling_id
id.description: Surrogate primary key: a dense sequential integer (1 to 87,769, no nulls, fully unique) identifying each ruling row. Carries no business meaning beyond row identity.

text.name: ruling_text
text.description: Full text of the official ruling explaining how the referenced card's abilities work or interact with the rules (e.g. 'Cycling is an activated ability...', 'Totem armor has no effect if the enchanted permanent is put into a graveyard...'). 19,593 distinct texts across 87,769 rows because the same ruling is stored once per printing of the card.

uuid.name: card_uuid
uuid.description: UUID of the card printing the ruling applies to; foreign key to cards.uuid (many-to-one, up to ~27 rulings per card). This is MTGJSON's per-printing card identifier, not a ruling identifier — the same ruling text/date recurs under the uuids of different printings of the same card.

table.name: set_translations
table.purpose: Localized (translated) names of Magic: The Gathering sets. Grain: one row per set × language (121 sets × 10 languages = 1210 rows). This is the translations side-table of 'sets' in an MTGJSON-style database (cards, foreign_data, legalities, rulings, sets); each row gives the name of one set in one of the ten languages MTG was printed in, or null when no translation exists. Evidence: setCode values are canonical MTG set codes (10E, 4ED, TSP, M14, RTR, EVE, ARC, C16, DDR) and translation values are those sets' names in the row's language (e.g. RTR → 'Ritorno a Ravnica' in Italian).

id.name: id
id.description: Surrogate primary key of the translation row. Sequential integers 1–1210 (min 1, max 1210, mean 605.5, perfectly uniform quartiles), unique across all 1210 rows; carries no meaning beyond row identity.

language.name: language
language.description: Language of the set-name translation. Exactly 10 distinct values, each occurring 121 times (once per set) — the languages Magic: The Gathering sets were localized into. Observed: Chinese Simplified, Chinese Traditional, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Russian; the remaining two are presumably Portuguese (Brazil) and Spanish, matching MTG's ten print languages (the sample translation 'Alvorecer' is Portuguese).

setCode.name: set_code
setCode.description: Code of the Magic: The Gathering set whose name is translated (e.g. 10E = Tenth Edition, 4ED = Fourth Edition, TSP = Time Spiral, M14 = Magic 2014, RTR = Return to Ravnica, EVE = Eventide, ARC = Archenemy, C16 = Commander 2016, DDR = Duel Decks: Nissa vs. Ob Nixilis). Foreign key to sets.code (many-to-one, join accepted by statistics); 121 distinct codes, each appearing once per language (10 times).

translation.name: translated_set_name
translation.description: The set's name rendered in the row's language. Evidence: RTR → 'Ritorno a Ravnica' (Italian), EVE → 'イーブンタイド' (Japanese for 'Eventide'), 'Ханы Таркиры' (Russian for Khans of Tarkir), 'Базовый выпуск Magic 2015' (Russian for 'Magic 2015 Core Set'), 'Terres natales' (French for Homelands). Null in ~19% of rows (≈231) where no translation exists for that set–language pair; English set names repeated across all 10 languages (e.g. 'Ajani vs. Nicol Bolas', 'Archenemy', 'Battle Royale', 'Beatdown') mark sets whose names were not localized.

table.name: Magic: The Gathering set catalogue
table.purpose: One row per Magic: The Gathering set/release (expansion, core set, promo series, deck product, memorabilia, etc.) - 551 sets spanning 1993-08-05 (Limited Edition Alpha, the first Magic set) to 2021-03-19. This is the MTGJSON set structure: the cards table references a set via cards.setCode, and set_translations holds localized set names. Columns carry the set's identity (code, name), sizing, release metadata, booster composition, and IDs for external vendors (Cardmarket, TCGplayer, Magic Online).

baseSetSize.name: Base set size
baseSetSize.description: Number of distinct cards in the set as released, excluding alternate printings/variants. Ranges 0-1694 (median 26); small values (1-6) are typical of promo sets, large ones of expansions/core sets. Always <= totalSetSize, and equal to it for sets without extra printings.

block.name: Block / product line
block.description: The Magic block or product family the set belongs to: true blocks ('Theros', 'Kamigawa', 'Scars of Mirrodin', 'Shadows over Innistrad') as well as series groupings for non-block products ('Core Set', 'Commander', 'Judge Gift Cards', 'Friday Night Magic', 'Magic Player Rewards'). Null for the ~51% of sets (mostly one-off promos/memorabilia) that belong to no block.

booster.name: Booster pack configuration
booster.description: Serialized JSON (stored as text) describing how the set's booster packs are composed: per-variant ('default', 'arena') lists of boosters with slot contents such as basic, common, uncommon, rare, rareMythic, land and special slots (e.g., double-faced card slots). The most common value is the standard 15-card draft booster (1 basic, 10 common, 3 uncommon, 1 rare/mythic). Null for the ~75% of sets sold without boosters (promos, duel decks, memorabilia).

code.name: Set code
code.description: Unique short code identifying the set (e.g., TSP = Time Spiral, 10E = Tenth Edition, PGRN = Guilds of Ravnica promos, PWP09 = Wizards Play Network 2009 promos). Natural key of the table: referenced by cards.setCode and set_translations.setCode.

id.name: Set ID (surrogate key)
id.description: Auto-increment surrogate primary key, sequential 1-551 with one value per set; carries no external meaning.

isFoilOnly.name: Foil-only flag
isFoilOnly.description: Boolean (0/1): 1 when every card in the set exists only in foil (167 sets, mostly promos and premium products); 0 otherwise.

isForeignOnly.name: Foreign-only flag
isForeignOnly.description: Boolean (0/1): 1 when the set was printed only in non-English languages (16 sets); 0 otherwise.

isNonFoilOnly.name: Non-foil-only flag
isNonFoilOnly.description: Boolean (0/1): 1 when the set's cards exist only in non-foil (106 sets); 0 otherwise. Counterpart of isFoilOnly.

isOnlineOnly.name: Online-only flag
isOnlineOnly.description: Boolean (0/1): 1 when the set exists only in digital form (Magic Online / MTG Arena), 26 sets; 0 otherwise.

isPartialPreview.name: Partial preview flag
isPartialPreview.description: Boolean (0/1): 1 when the set was only partially previewed/spoiled, i.e., its full card list was not yet known when the data was captured (exactly 1 set, presumably the most recent release); 0 otherwise.

keyruneCode.name: Keyrune set-symbol code
keyruneCode.description: Code for the Keyrune icon font used to render the set's symbol/logo. Equals the set's own code for sets with a unique symbol (TSP, ALL, M14, ARC); promo and miscellaneous sets share generic icons (PMEI, DCI, DEFAULT, PARL, PMPS), which is why only 249 distinct values exist for 551 sets.

mcmId.name: Cardmarket set ID
mcmId.description: Magic Card Market (Cardmarket) expansion ID for the set; unique among non-null values, null for the ~64% of sets Cardmarket does not catalogue (promos, memorabilia).

mcmIdExtras.name: Cardmarket extras-set ID
mcmIdExtras.description: Cardmarket ID of the set's separate 'Extras' entry, used when Cardmarket splits a set's supplementary cards into their own expansion; populated for only 10 sets, with values in the same ID range as mcmId.

mcmName.name: Cardmarket set name
mcmName.description: The set's name as listed on Magic Card Market (e.g., 'Aether Revolt', 'Zendikar Expeditions', 'Portal Second Age'); unique, null exactly where mcmId is null.

mtgoCode.name: Magic Online set code
mtgoCode.description: The set's code as used in Magic Online, which can differ from the main set code (e.g., V10, PR, DRB); null for the ~71% of sets not available on MTGO.

name.name: Set name
name.description: Full human-readable name of the set (e.g., 'Ultimate Masters', 'Magic 2010', 'Mirrodin Promos', 'World Championship Decks 2000'); unique across all 551 rows.

parentCode.name: Parent set code
parentCode.description: Set code of the parent release this set belongs to (e.g., several promo/token sets point at ZNR = Zendikar Rising, BFZ = Battle for Zendikar, BNG/FRF/JOU = Theros-block expansions); null for standalone sets (~72%).

releaseDate.name: Release date
releaseDate.description: The set's release date in ISO YYYY-MM-DD format (stored as text). Spans 1993-08-05 (Limited Edition Alpha, the first Magic set) to 2021-03-19, the snapshot's most recent release; many promo sets carry a nominal January 1 or December 1 date.

tcgplayerGroupId.name: TCGplayer group ID
tcgplayerGroupId.description: TCGplayer product-group ID for the set (TCGplayer groups products by set); null for ~53% of sets. The most frequent value, 62, is shared by 21 sets, so some IDs are catch-all groups covering several sets rather than one per set.

totalSetSize.name: Total set size
totalSetSize.description: Total number of cards in the set counting every printing/variant; always >= baseSetSize (mean 102.6 vs 99.6) and equal to it for sets without alternate printings. Ranges 0-1694, median 26.

type.name: Set type
type.description: Category of the release: promo (234 sets), expansion (87), memorabilia (34), box (27), duel_deck (27), plus rarer kinds such as premium_deck, draft_innovation, archenemy, spellbook (20 distinct types in total).
